extracted.intended_audience: ALSC award committee chairs and members (John Newbery Medal and related award committees)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and evaluative guidelines for members and chairs of the ALSC John Newbery Medal (and related) award committees, covering eligibility, meeting conduct, nominations, discussion, balloting, conflicts of interest, and administrative responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting attendance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Be able to attend all required discussion and decision meetings, in person and virtual, scheduled for the year of service, including pre-scheduled virtual meetings for a week in July following the Annual conference, virtual meetings in the two weeks prior to the LibLearnX Conference, and the in-person final selection meeting at LibLearnX, and be able to follow procedures established by the committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A committee member must tender their resignation if they are unable to attend a required meeting, regardless of reason. For virtual meetings ensure calendar cleared, necessary technology, and any employer permission/time-off. For LibLearnX in-person meeting, secure supervisor permission, funding, hotel/transportation, conference registration, and notify Chair of emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Have ready access to the major part of the current output of children’s books under consideration in outlets such as their local library or bookstore and through interlibrary loan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occasional unavailable titles are recognized; arrangements for review copies may be made per committee guidelines (Relationship with Publishers). Committee members accept appointment with understanding they have access to new books; ultimately it is each member’s responsibility to obtain such books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of service limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: No individual may serve on the Batchelder Award, Caldecott Medal, Geisel Award, Newbery Medal, Sibert Medal, Legacy Award, or Notable Children’s Books Committee more often than once every four years; the four-year period begins from last year of term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule does not apply to appointment for Chair or to other ALSC committees. May be suspended for emergency mid-year replacements to provide flexibility. Violation may result in dismissal and preclusion from future committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship with publishers — acceptance of unsolicited books
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members may accept unsolicited books sent by publishers for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members are not to solicit publishers for free personal copies; they may accept unsolicited offers but should avoid soliciting favors or invitations. If unsolicited offers are accepted, they must not influence how books are considered or final choices made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship with publishers — roster and shipping
rubrics_metrics.description: Chair consults members to verify addresses for publishers and makes a roster for publishers; ALSC Awards Coordinator makes roster available to publishers as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses should be viable for term of service because changing a mailing address with warehouses is difficult. Chair surveys which books have not been received and may contact publishers directly for needed titles; PGC assumes role toward end of deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of conflicts of interest with publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members are cautioned to avoid any conflicts of interest that might grow out of personal contact with personnel involved in publishing children’s books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacts need not be suspended so long as there is express understanding contacts do not influence consideration or final choices. Committee members must resign immediately on development of any circumstance that disqualifies them or gives appearance of affecting impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher submission procedures and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers should review terms/criteria and submit one copy of the work to the award committee Chair (optionally to each committee member). The deadline for submitting books for consideration is December 31 of the publication year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of committee members is available via Terms and Criteria page. Guidelines and submission procedures are outlined on the ALSC website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of self-published and small-press titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-published and small-press books are eligible provided they meet all other eligibility requirements and are eligible in their first year of publication only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a self-published book is later republished by another publisher commercially, it will not be reconsidered. Chair keeps/passes on a current year’s list of award-eligible books received directly from authors or small presses. Sharing of these titles with committee is at Chair’s discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair responsibilities — calendar and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Chair establishes and distributes a calendar of the year’s work and meetings as soon as possible and establishes ground rules for all forms of committee communication at the beginning of the term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair schedules meetings (virtual and in-person), sets agendas, appoints secretary, shares discussion lists and late additions promptly, communicates logistical needs to Awards Coordinator by October 1, and may prepare materials (table tents, laptop/tablet arrangements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of virtual vs electronic communication
rubrics_metrics.description: A video conferencing platform will be used for virtual meetings; electronic communication will be used to facilitate distribution of information and regular discussion of procedural issues. Substantial book discussions among committee members will be limited to in-person or virtual committee meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email is not used for substantive discussion and is not a substitute for face-to-face or virtual book discussions. Email may be used for eligibility or factual-error matters and those questions are directed to the Chair to decide if they should go to the full committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation — study terms/criteria and reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members are urged to prepare by reading the committee manual (especially terms, criteria, definitions), books/articles on evaluation and criticism, and by practising writing critical viewpoints and analyses of past winners structured around award terms/criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Appendix A Reading Lists and attend/listen to book discussions (especially those with children) where appropriate. Practice improves application of award factors and helps clarify thinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying eligible books
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members are responsible for identifying eligible books via publisher catalogs, review journals, publishing announcements, ALSC Notable Children’s Books lists, and attending Notables deliberations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin early; publication pace increases through the year. Contact Notable committee members or visit ALSC website for leads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining eligible books — acceptable sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members should obtain eligible books via publisher mailings, galleys at conferences, review copies received at workplace, and browsing new titles at bookstores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members are not to solicit publishers for copies (see Relationship to Publishers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining eligibility — focus on current terms not precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members should refer to the current terms, criteria, and definitions (including Appendix B) rather than to precedent or past winners when determining eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make initial effort to determine eligibility of publisher and author/illustrator: year of publication, citizenship/residency (U.S. required), and locale of publisher (must be located in the U.S.). Sources include publishers’ catalogs, websites, Library of Congress, Amazon. Ambiguous cases: notify Chair, who consults with PGC and informs committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading responsibilities and re-reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members are responsible for identifying, obtaining, and reading eligible books throughout the year; the reading load is heavy and re-reading is often required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin early and keep up; re-reading may reveal strengths missed on first read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note-taking standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a convenient note-taking system that speaks to the award criteria, including complete bibliographic information, a short summary, a critical statement noting strengths and weaknesses, and references to specific page numbers and/or quoted passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes should be succinct and specific to clarify thinking and aid discussion. Form may be file cards, binders, electronic (but public tools like Goodreads should not be used). Chair may ask members to share note-taking ideas. Sample Note-Taking Form in Appendix C. Collecting professional reviews is acceptable but reviews are not to be quoted during discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestion process — monthly anonymous suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting early, the Chair solicits suggestions monthly via an online tool; suggestions are compiled in a table listing suggested books and number of suggestions; after the second round a cumulative list is provided. Suggestions remain anonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No set limit on number suggested, but members are urged not to overload the list. Suggest all books deemed strong contenders based on award criteria. Members may recommend books previously suggested to develop gauge of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination process — three rounds and justification statements
rubrics_metrics.description: In autumn the Chair requests three rounds of nominations: three, two, and two books (total seven distinct nominations) with complete bibliographic information and justification statements usually no more than 100 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members may not repeat nominations across rounds but may nominate titles nominated by others. Nominations are submitted via online tool and remain anonymous. Justifications prepare members for oral discussion and succinctly state points that speak to award criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Discussion Meeting practices
rubrics_metrics.description: A required virtual Initial Discussion Meeting (after Annual Conference) includes practice book discussion, review of terms/criteria/definitions, procedures for the year, and review of member responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair sets agenda, appoints secretary, selects short list of suggested titles for practice, and asks select members to introduce books. Practice discussion uses same guidelines as selection to make it meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book discussion conduct guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: During selection discussions use critical analysis and avoid plot summaries and generalities; be clear, concise, audible, courteous, and avoid personal anecdotes; refer back to criteria; make comparisons only to other eligible books; focus first on strengths before weaknesses; be even-handed; conclude with closing statement from the introducer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep contributions additive (avoid repetition). Include specific evidence (page references/quotations). See referenced articles for additional best practices (Thom’s Rules of Order; CCBC guidelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minutes and record-keeping rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary takes minutes on order of business and procedural matters; no notes are taken on practice book discussions. At LibLearnX secretary turns in minutes to Chair; Chair turns minutes and Quarterly Report to Executive Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly Reports are submitted during the year with minutes attached using ALSC staff-provided link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary deliberations purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning early January, virtual preliminary deliberations are held to discuss nominated titles and make initial cuts by consensus guiding the Chair's LibLearnX discussion list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions guide the Chair in establishing the final discussion list for LibLearnX; ensure books for discussion are read in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: LibLearnX Selection Meeting procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: In-person final selection meeting where Chair establishes discussion list (nominated titles remaining after preliminary deliberations plus late suggestions), members introduce selected books, full discussion of each book occurs, and then selection ballot is held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair provides list at least three weeks prior (additions up to one week prior). Members expected to bring books, notes, and biographical info. Discussion order ordinarily alphabetical by author unless grouping similar titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balloting point system and winner formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members list first, second, and third place votes in an online tool. The tool assigns 4 points to each first-place vote, 3 points to each second-place vote, and 2 points to each third-place vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A book must receive at least eight first-choice votes (4 points each for total >= 32 points) and must have an eight-point lead over the book with next-highest points to win. If committee is operating an odd number down, Chair is recommended to refrain from voting. Awards Coordinator can adjust formula if committee is even number down.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-balloting procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee may not proceed to another ballot without a second round of book discussion. By consensus the committee may withdraw books that received no votes or minimal support from the discussion list; once withdrawn a book is permanently eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After re-discussion, proceed to second ballot using same point system and formula. If no winner after second ballot, re-open discussion and alternate discussion and re-balloting until a winner is selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor Books selection principles
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no requirement to name Honor Books and no rule on number; Honor Books are expected to be truly distinguished, not merely strong contenders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee first decides whether to name Honor Books. If yes, options include using the winning selection ballot to consider titles with next-highest points or conducting one additional ballot consisting of titles from winning ballot that received points (winner eliminated). Only one additional Honor ballot allowed; titles with no remaining support may be withdrawn by consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation and vacancy filling
rubrics_metrics.description: A member must resign immediately upon development of any circumstance disqualifying them or affecting impartiality or if unable to attend required meeting. Resignations must be sent to Chair, President, and Executive Director; Chair resignations go to committee, PGC, President, Executive Director and require forwarding current files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a member resigns, President appoints replacement and may draw from Notable Children’s Books Committee if timing is close to LibLearnX. If no suitable replacement found in time, committee will operate one member down and reformulate voting procedure accordingly.
